note: Written here, not into lean/registry/open-questions/, because that folder belongs to another agent. One record per file is what the schema expects; these are bundled so they can be split without reshaping. content_hash is sha256 over the canonical JSON of the hashed fields, computed the same way the registry computes a law hash.

requirements.statement_en: The neutral equilibrium heterozygosity law (HET1) is a well-formed declarative row but reads cannot-evaluate for every design sim-engine can produce.
requirements.not_checkable_because: The engine's design vocabulary (sim-engine/lib/state.mjs and sim-engine/lib/perturb-map.mjs) is morphological, thermal, hydrostatic and metabolic: body_mass_kg, SL_m/standard_length_m, pectoral_span_m, airspeed_m_s, critical_swimming_speed_m_s, body_temperature_C, water_temperature_C, salinity_psu, depth_m, altitude_m, cardiac and intake/routine-cost terms. None of the quantities this law constrains appear in it.
requirements.would_constrain_if_supplied: Rejects a design whose declared neutral heterozygosity is not the mutation-drift equilibrium of its declared effective size and mutation rate, or is outside (0,1). A population-level annotation on a design would be enough; no new measurement of the organism is needed.

requirements.statement_en: Hamilton's rule has NO rule-out direction over a design and was deliberately given no browser_check row. This is not a missing-input problem: supplying r, b and c would not make it bind.
requirements.not_checkable_because: The law classifies the DIRECTION of change in a social trait. A row with op gt on r*b > c would report violated whenever a trait is predicted to DECREASE, and a costly trait that kin selection disfavours is an ordinary organism, not an impossible one. In a surface where red means "violates a law" that is a false positive, so no block was declared. The rejected block is kept in the law's meta under browser_check_absent.block_considered_and_rejected.
requirements.would_constrain_if_supplied: Nothing, as a design-level rule-out. It would become checkable only against a design that explicitly CLAIMS a social trait is maintained by kin selection; then r*b <= c refutes that claim. That is a claim-level check and the registry has no place for one today - which is itself a gap worth recording.

failed_theorems.statement_en: A neutral mutant destined to fix takes on average about 4*Ne generations, which exceeds the mean time to loss 2*(Ne/N)*ln(2N) at every population size, so the two timescales separate without bound.
failed_theorems.reason: written but never compiled: I ran out of lake-lock window. The statement is believed provable but has NOT been checked by Lean, so it must not be read as a result.
failed_theorems.what_was_tried: The plan was: named hypothesis t_fix = 4*Ne and t_loss = 2*(Ne/N)*Real.log (2*N); the timescale separation reduces to 4*N > 2*Real.log (2*N) for N >= 1, which follows from Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos (log x <= x - 1 gives log (2N) <= 2N - 1, hence 2*log(2N) <= 4N - 2 < 4N). No Lean file was written.
failed_theorems.what_survives: The claim itself, its source (Kimura M, Ohta T (1969) Genetics 61:763, doi:10.1093/genetics/61.3.763) and the reduction above. Anyone picking this up starts from the stated inequality, not from scratch.

failed_theorems.statement_en: Hamilton's selection gradient on age-specific survival, s(a) = (1/T) * sum over x > a of exp(-r*x)*l_x*m_x, is non-increasing in a, strictly decreasing while reproduction continues, and zero after the last age of reproduction.
failed_theorems.reason: written but never compiled: judged too likely to need several build cycles while three other agents were contending for the single lake lock. Not attempted in Lean.
failed_theorems.what_was_tried: The plan was a Finset tail sum over ages with non-negative terms, monotone by Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg, strict where the term is positive, and zero past the last reproductive age by Finset.sum_eq_zero. The hard part is the index arithmetic on Finset.Icc, not the biology.
failed_theorems.what_survives: The claim, its source (Hamilton WD (1966) The moulding of senescence by natural selection. J Theor Biol 12:12-45, doi:10.1016/0022-5193(66)90184-6) and the proof plan. Note the claim's own context records that the INEVITABILITY half is refuted (doi:10.1038/nature12789, negligible senescence in some species), so only the monotonicity should ever be formalised - a law asserting inevitability would assert a refuted claim.

failed_theorems.statement_en: Where cell-cell surface tension exceeds cell-medium tension, the external angle between neighbouring cells is below 120 degrees; where cell-cell tension equals or exceeds the sum of the other two, the cells touch only at a point.
failed_theorems.reason: abandoned for lack of lake-lock time, not for any difficulty found. This is the strongest unproposed candidate in the whole queue head: two exact bounds with their thresholds, from a force balance.
failed_theorems.what_was_tried: Nothing attempted in Lean. The statement is a two-part inequality over three tensions and an angle; a Lean version would be of the same order as the turing-ddi candidate that did land.
failed_theorems.what_survives: The claim thompson1917-ch03 (Thompson 1917 On Growth and Form, ch. VII, record thompson1917-ch07-06 in docs/claims.json) and this adjudication. It is the first thing the next round should pick up.

failed_theorems.statement_en: The liquid coating of a spider's spiral thread, being a liquid cylinder, is unstable once its length exceeds its circumference, and breaks into equal, equally spaced beads.
failed_theorems.reason: abandoned for lack of lake-lock time. An exact bound (L > 2*pi*r) with a clean impossibility reading; the observed spacing exceeds the theoretical value because of viscosity and drag on the core thread, which the claim states and a law must not hide.
failed_theorems.what_survives: The claim (record thompson1917-ch05-12) and the bound L > 2*pi*r. The honest law would prove the instability threshold only, and name the viscosity correction as the reason observed spacing is larger.

failed_theorems.statement_en: Because the impulse of a leap is proportional to muscle volume and so to body mass, take-off velocity is independent of body size, so similarly built animals jump to the same absolute height rather than the same relative height.
failed_theorems.reason: abandoned for lack of lake-lock time. Worth singling out: it is the only Thompson item in the queue head whose quantities the engine nearly supplies (body_mass_kg and a speed), so it is the best CHECKABLE candidate left in the corpus.

The scaling argument is two lines; the work is choosing an honest named hypothesis for "impulse proportional to muscle volume", and the claim itself concedes that longer levers give larger animals some advantage, which a law must not suppress.
failed_theorems.what_survives: The claim (record thompson1917-ch02-09) and the observation that it is the most checkable remaining candidate.

failed_theorems.statement_en: Under local mate competition with n foundresses on a patch whose offspring mate before the daughters disperse, the evolutionarily stable sex ratio is female-biased, (n-1)/2n, and the bias weakens as n grows.

It contradicts the scope of the fisher-sex-ratio candidate that did land, and the right outcome is for propose.mjs to record the two as CONTESTED with both ids, not for me to leave the tension in a prose scope sentence.
failed_theorems.what_was_tried: Nothing attempted in Lean. The ESS ratio is an explicit function of n, so the statement is of the same order as the candidates that landed.
failed_theorems.what_survives: The claim (hamilton-lmc, math-bio-theorems/claims/key-claims.json, Hamilton WD 1967) and the reason: this is the highest-value next proposal in the corpus, BECAUSE it should produce a contested pair rather than a ninth agreeable candidate. A law set whose laws never conflict has not been tested.

failed_theorems.statement_en: A micrococcus 0.15 micrometres across contains only some tens of thousands of protein molecules, so organisms cannot be much smaller than the smallest already known.
failed_theorems.reason: NEEDS-A-MISSING-CONSTANT, and it is the single highest-value missing constant found this round. The statement is a clean impossibility (a minimum diameter from a minimum molecule count and a molecular volume) and exactly ONE number is absent: the volume of a protein molecule. The claim does not give it and the repo does not hold it.
failed_theorems.what_was_tried: Nothing attempted in Lean, because a law built on a guessed molecular volume would be a fabricated constant, which is worse than no law.
failed_theorems.what_survives: The claim (record thompson1917-ch02-18), the reduction (minimum diameter follows from minimum molecule count times molecular volume, as a cube root), and the precise request: a sourced mean volume per protein molecule. Supply that and this becomes a proposable impossibility bound.

failed_theorems.statement_en: The biconcave mammalian red blood corpuscle is not a surface of constant mean curvature, so it cannot be a fluid drop in equilibrium under surface tension alone; some other force maintains its shape.
failed_theorems.reason: abandoned on cost, not on doubt. It is a genuine impossibility and would be a fine law, but it needs the differential geometry of surfaces of revolution (mean curvature) in Lean, an order of magnitude beyond the algebraic candidates of this round.
failed_theorems.what_survives: The claim (record thompson1917-ch05-24) and the cost assessment, so the next agent does not rediscover it as cheap.
